regeln: Prioritize genuine tool demonstrations: always show real interface screens or README media; avoid generic illustrations or symbolic icons when actual assets exist.
Ensure each visual motif matches the spoken content: every shot must directly illustrate the action or feature being described, not just a decorative placeholder.
Include at least 18 distinct, relevant motifs in every 35–45‑second Short, counting only unique subjects or actions—exclude simple zooms, crops, or background changes.

Structure scripts with a clear problem-solution arc: dedicate sentences to the manual bottleneck/pain point, explain the logical link between tools (e.g., 'reasoning brain'), and provide a tangible, actionable payoff.
Keep the black‑haired presenter (leather jacket, cyan glasses) present throughout; in key shots, the tool logo and branding must dominate over the presenter’s image to ensure visual hierarchy.
Use the painted open‑world‑game aesthetic for all fictional scenes; avoid real‑world stock clips or copied game characters, and ensure visual warmth and high detail density.
Maintain factual accuracy by referencing primary documentation; explain the human task and workflow rather than reading benchmark claims, architecture tags, or parameter counts.
Include the mandatory spoken “like, share, save” CTA at its designated format‑specific position; do not replace it with another request.

Keep script pacing appropriate to format: short videos require faster motion and frequent motif changes, while long videos allow for deliberate, longer demonstrations; avoid cross-pollinating pacing styles.
Verify all scripts against primary sources before finalizing to prevent reliance on unverified features or incorrect claims.
Use the video hook to promise a specific, tangible task-based benefit within the first three seconds to ensure immediate viewer relevance.
Do not over‑generalize from a single review or image defect; treat each piece of feedback as data and phrase lessons conditionally to improve story flow, suspense, and surprise factors.

produktionsdiagnosen.quelle: GitHub-Produktionsbericht, Skript und Joblog; kein Nutzerqualitaetsurteil
befunde: Generatives Sprachmodell und nicht-generative Entscheidungsmodelle wurden unter Hallucination-Free AI zusammengefasst.
Faktenpruefer verwarfen mehrere Story-Ueberarbeitungen wegen unbelegter Detail-/Hardwareaussagen.
Im gespeicherten Entwurf bleibt single forward pass als unbelegter Detailhinweis stehen.
Der Kritiker schlug eine neue Null-Halluzinations-Garantie und andere Tools vor; diese Vorschlaege sind keine Quellen.
Kein Video erzeugt, keine Video-Note und keine Telegram-Videozustellung.
